title: Pointer Arithmetic
concept: Adding to a pointer moves to the 'next slot', not just +1 in address!

steps.title: Including stdio.h Header
steps.explanation:
Header for using `printf`.

The key lesson here is that adding 1 to a pointer advances the address by `sizeof(type)`, not just 1.

steps.title: Defining the main Function
steps.explanation:
The main frame is created and the array `arr` and pointer `p` are prepared.

The pointer `p` will point to array elements sequentially to read their values.

steps.title: Array Declaration
steps.explanation:
Array `arr` stores 10, 20, 30 in contiguous memory.

Thanks to this contiguity, pointer arithmetic can accurately locate the next element.

steps.title: Initializing the Pointer to the Array Start
steps.explanation:
In `int *p = arr;`, `arr` decays to `&arr[0]` and is stored in `p`.

So `p` becomes a pointer pointing to the first element.

steps.title: Pointer Dereferencing
steps.explanation:
`*p` reads the value of the element `p` currently points to.

At the start, it points to the first element, so the result is the value of `arr[0]`.

steps.title: Pointer Arithmetic 1: p + 1
steps.explanation:
`p + 1` moves to the next element's address. The actual offset is `sizeof(int)` bytes.

So `*(p+1)` equals the value of the second element.

steps.title: Pointer Arithmetic 2: p + 2
steps.explanation:
By the same principle, `*(p+2)` reads the third element.

To summarize: `*(p+n)` behaves identically to `arr[n]`.

steps.title: Program Termination
steps.explanation:
`return 0;` ends the program.

The key formula: `p+n` translates to `p + n*sizeof(type)` in actual addresses.

quiz.question: If int *p = 1000; what is the value of p + 2? (int is 4 bytes)

misconceptions.wrong: Writing *p+1 instead of *(p+1) is the same
misconceptions.why:
`*p + 1` means (*p's value) + 1, i.e., adding 1 to the value, while `*(p+1)` reads the value at the next address.
Parentheses are critical.

keyTakeaway: Adding 1 to a pointer advances the memory address by `sizeof(type)`. (jump to the next slot)
